exercise.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Wrist Curl
library_steps: Rest one forearm on a bench, palm up, hand over the edge.
Lower the dumbbell by bending your wrist, then curl it up.
Finish your reps, then switch arms.
exercise.one_line_summary: Seated, one forearm along the thigh palm up with the hand past the knee; the wrist bends down, then curls the dumbbell up. Wrist flexors on the palm side of the forearm do the work.

setup.target: Forearm resting on the thigh, palm up, wrist just past the knee.

muscles.anatomy: Flexor carpi radialis, flexor carpi ulnaris
muscles.emg: Not measured in this exercise; loaded wrist flexion trains the flexor group (TY14).

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: The elbows or forearms move as the wrist works.
mistakes.why_it_matters: The wrist muscles must do the lift alone.

sources.citation: Tyler TF, Nicholas SJ, Schmitt BM, Mullaney M, Hogan DE. 2014. Clinical outcomes of the addition of eccentrics for rehabilitation of previously failed treatments of golfers elbow. Int J Sports Phys Ther.
sources.what_it_gave: Isolated loaded wrist-flexion exercise used to strengthen the wrist flexors (palm side of the forearm).

sources.citation: Lung BE, Siwiec RM. 2024. Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Forearm Flexor Carpi Ulnaris Muscle. StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf).
sources.what_it_gave: Flexor carpi ulnaris: superficial palm-side forearm muscle, the most powerful wrist flexor.
